title: The Emperor's Cracked Mirror (KN)
summary: Akbar smashes a mirror in anger when it distorts his reflection. Birbal uses the broken shards to teach the court a lesson on emotional self-control.
full_text:
In the imperial bedchamber, Emperor Akbar was dressing for an important diplomatic summit when he looked into a large, imported Venetian looking-glass. The glass had developed an invisible hairline crack during transit, causing Akbar's reflection to appear twisted, with a distorted nose and crooked eyes!

In sudden frustration and vanity, Akbar struck the mirror with his royal staff, shattering it into a hundred shards upon the marble floor: 'Ugly, lying glass! How dare you distort my face!'

Birbal entered the chamber and observed the broken glass and the breathing Emperor.

Birbal knelt down, picked up one of the jagged shards from the floor, and looked into it.

'Birbal,' Akbar complained, 'that mirror made me look like a monster!'

Birbal held the shard before the Emperor with serene gentleness:

'Sire, look into this single broken piece now that your anger has cooled. What do you see?'

Akbar looked down. In the small shard, his reflection appeared calm, handsome, and clear.

Birbal said:

'Sire, when you struck the mirror in anger, it was not the glass that was distorted; it was your own impatient mind!

'When the mind is agitated by wrath, pride, or fear, the entire world appears hostile, twisted, and ugly. We blame our ministers, our servants, our wives, and our friends, striking out to break them like this mirror.

'Yet the moment we breathe deeply and quiet the storm within our own breast, the world reflects our own calm dignity once again.

'A ruler must never deliver judgments when his mind is cracked by anger, for he will punish his own distorted reflection instead of the truth.'

Akbar sat down in silence, deeply moved by the reminder. He apologized to his servants, ordered a new mirror placed in his chamber, and thanked Birbal for being the guardian of his emotional peace.
